newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso rises as foreign fund outflows end.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso rises as foreign fund outflows end.

text.p: The Philippine peso strengthened by almost one centavo to close at 26.265 to the dollar from yesterday's 26.274 as demand for dollars eased, traders said.
A trader said the outflow of foreign funds has stopped, following the sharp rise in the local bourse early Wednesday.
Foreign banks have been buying up dollars in the past days, remitting portfolio funds out of the bearish stock market.
Another trader said the dollar selldown was also triggered by the Central Bank which adjusted its selling rate from 26.270 pesos yesterday to 26.266 in the afternoon.
"Banks took that as a cue to sell their dollars, before they become too cheap," he added.

After the initial selldown, the Central Bank went into buying mode to keep the peso from rising abruptly. It started buying dollars when the rate hit the intra-day high of 26.262. Its buying rates vary from 26.263 to 26.264.
Traders expected the peso to remain stable due to the Central Bank intervention. - RAMONCITO DELA CRUZ 63 2 8418938
